speaker_role: independent essay coach (College Essay Guy, runs an essay-resource business)
commercial_incentive: Channel promotes his website and resources; light plug only, no hard sell in this video.
key_insights: A personal statement need not center on a challenge; hardship can be mentioned briefly and woven in rather than dominating.
He frames the purpose as showing skills, qualities, values and interests you would bring to campus.
Five qualities to aim for: core values, surprising insight, vulnerability, visible craft over drafts, and sensory detail across several senses.
To find insight, go through each paragraph and repeatedly ask 'so what' until you reach something that surprises you.
Aim for moderate vulnerability, roughly 6-7 out of 10, and have a trusted person rate the draft on that scale.
Check which sense dominates (usually sight) and add smell, taste or touch; abstract language often hides missing detail.
Show the draft to only one or two trusted people.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker says strong essays he has seen went through at least five revisions.
Speaker suggests target vulnerability of about 6-7 on a 10-point scale (5-8 acceptable).
notable_or_distinctive: Walks through a full sample montage essay on multiple identities and annotates where each quality appears; the vulnerability-rating exercise is distinctive.
reliability_notes: Numbers are personal heuristics, not admissions data; auto-captions mostly clean with one censored word.
